page.title: Course Overview
page.contents:
MINDFUL LEARNING ACADEMY • CREATIVE WRITING • COURSE ORIENTATION

Course Overview

Creative Writing

MLA Course Code: CW

Credit: 1.0 High School Elective or English Language Arts Credit, as assigned

Course Type: Online, asynchronous, mastery-based

Delivery: 100% online through Moodle

Instructional Model: Writer’s workshop, craft study, revision, and publication

Teacher Support: Teacher of Record (TOR)

Course Description

Creative Writing develops voice, narrative craft, fiction, poetry, workshop, revision, and publication. You will study models, analyze purpose and craft, practice with structured support, create original responses or products, and revise using evidence and feedback.

Moodle contains the official instructional sequence, readings and media, required submissions, quizzes, unit assessments, grades, TOR feedback, and progress tracking.

Course Learning Outcomes

By the end of this course, you will be able to:

  • read, view, or listen closely for central ideas, details, structure, and purpose;
  • use relevant evidence accurately and explain how it supports a claim or creative choice;
  • analyze audience, context, perspective, language, and craft;
  • plan, draft, revise, edit, and publish clear work for an identified purpose;
  • evaluate sources for credibility, relevance, bias, and appropriate use;
  • communicate ideas effectively in written, oral, visual, or digital forms;
  • apply feedback and reflect on growth toward mastery.

Prerequisite Knowledge and Skills

You should be able to follow multistep directions, read grade-appropriate texts with support, write complete responses, organize work, use basic digital tools, and communicate with your TOR when assistance is needed.

Course Organization

This course contains 6 units and 48 lessons. Each unit contains eight lessons. Lessons 1–7 develop content and communication skills; Lesson 8 serves as unit synthesis. Each unit begins with an ungraded Unit Pretest and ends with a graded Unit Assessment.

  •  
  • Unit 1 — Foundations of Creative Writing, Voice, and Craft
  •  
  • Unit 2 — Narrative Craft, Point of View, Character, and Setting
  •  
  • Unit 3 — Fiction, Theme, Adaptation, and World Building
  •  
  • Unit 4 — Poetry, Figurative Language, Mood, and Style
  •  
  • Unit 5 — Revision, Workshop, Portfolio, and Publication
  •  
  • Unit 6 — Author Portfolio, Presentation, and Publication Synthesis

How Lessons Work

Each lesson follows a clear six-page learning sequence:

  1. Lesson Overview
  2. Vocabulary and Definitions
  3. Lesson
  4. Worked Example
  5. Independent Work
  6. Checkpoint

Complete the required notebook or process evidence and checkpoint submission separately. Lessons 1–7 include a Lesson Quiz; Lesson 8 is a synthesis lesson.

Notebook and Process Evidence

Maintain organized evidence identified in each lesson. It may include annotations, vocabulary, notes, source analysis, outlines, planning, drafts, rehearsal notes, peer- or self-review, revisions, and reflection. Submit only the evidence requested on the current page.

Assessments and Mastery

  • ungraded Unit Pretests;
  • required notebook or process-evidence submissions;
  • Mastery Checkpoints;
  • Lesson Quizzes for Lessons 1–7;
  • graded Unit Assessments.

The minimum mastery threshold is 80%. Revision, remediation, or approved reassessment may be required before progression.

Standards Alignment

Creative Writing uses MLA-created standards as the controlling curriculum standards, crosswalked to applicable Florida B.E.S.T. ELA standards, Common Core, SAT, ACT, communication and media-literacy expectations, and college- and career-readiness skills.

Teacher of Record Support

Your TOR monitors progress, grades required evidence, provides feedback, supports remediation, and assists with academic or technical problems. Include the course, unit, lesson, page title, and a specific question when requesting help.

Academic Integrity and Course Completion

Submit your own work. Do not copy, share assessment answers, fabricate sources or evidence, or submit unapproved AI-generated work as your own. The course is complete after all units, lessons, required evidence, checkpoints, quizzes, assessments, and directed revisions are finished.

page.title: How This Course Works
page.contents:
MINDFUL LEARNING ACADEMY • CREATIVE WRITING • COURSE ORIENTATION

How This Course Works

Mastery-Based Learning

Progress follows this cycle: Learn → Analyze → Practice → Apply → Check Mastery → Review Feedback → Revise when required. Completion depends on demonstrated understanding, not simply viewing pages.

Where You Begin

Begin each unit with its ungraded Unit Pretest. Complete it honestly and independently so your TOR can identify prior knowledge and skills that may need support.

Unit Workflow

  1. Complete the Unit Pretest.
  2. Work through lessons in the Moodle order.
  3. Complete every page and required evidence submission.
  4. Complete each Mastery Checkpoint and Lesson Quiz.
  5. Review TOR feedback and revise when directed.
  6. Complete the Unit Assessment.

Lesson Workflow

  1. Lesson Overview: read the lesson focus, standards, learning goals, workflow, and success criteria.
  2. Vocabulary and Definitions: learn and record the key terms needed for the lesson.
  3. Lesson: study the content, craft explanations, models, visuals, and teacher guidance.
  4. Worked Example: follow step-by-step modeling that explains how a writer makes and evaluates craft choices.
  5. Independent Work: apply the lesson skills to a substantial reading, analysis, or original composition task.
  6. Checkpoint: independently demonstrate the lesson target and submit the required responses.

Text and Source Evidence

When a task requires a text, image, audio/video selection, chart, or source excerpt, the necessary material must appear or be linked on the same page. Cite or reference the evidence accurately and explain its significance. Do not rely on memory of an earlier page.

Worked Example

Study each model in order. Follow the teacher reasoning, notice how each craft decision affects the reader, and use the demonstrated process when you begin your independent work.

Independent Work

Complete the assigned response, composition, report, or presentation work independently. Address the purpose and audience, use relevant evidence or craft choices, and revise for clarity and correctness.

Checkpoint

Read the current checkpoint task, complete it independently, and submit the requested evidence. The checkpoint is separate from notebook or general practice work. Review feedback after grading and revise only when directed.

Lesson Quizzes and Unit Assessments

Lessons 1–7 include a Lesson Quiz; Lesson 8 is synthesis. Unit Assessments measure understanding, analysis, evidence use, application, and communication across the unit. Required stimuli appear with the question that uses them.

Completion, Mastery, and Help

The minimum mastery threshold is 80%. A page view alone is not completion. Contact your TOR with the course, unit, lesson, page title, what you attempted, and the exact assistance needed.

page.title: Expectations and Policies
page.contents:
MINDFUL LEARNING ACADEMY • CREATIVE WRITING • COURSE ORIENTATION

Expectations and Policies

Student Responsibilities

  • follow the official Moodle sequence;
  • read all directions before beginning;
  • complete and submit original work;
  • use evidence and show reasoning;
  • review feedback and revise when required;
  • communicate promptly and respectfully;
  • protect assessment integrity and account security.

Grading and Feedback

Your TOR grades required evidence and assessments using the stated criteria. Feedback may identify missing evidence, an inaccurate interpretation, weak organization, a craft or delivery issue, or a need for remediation. Read all feedback before revising.

Work Evidence

Label evidence with the unit, lesson, and task. Upload the requested file type and confirm that text, annotations, planning, drafts, images, or recordings are complete and readable or playable.

Mastery Checkpoint Evidence

Checkpoint work must answer the task on the current page. Include the requested claim, evidence, reasoning, analysis, craft explanation, reflection, or presentation evidence. Do not submit unrelated notes.

Evidence and Communication Expectations

  • identify the source, speaker, text, or context accurately;
  • select specific and relevant evidence;
  • explain how evidence supports the response;
  • organize ideas logically for the purpose and audience;
  • use appropriate conventions, attribution, and citation;
  • revise content and edit presentation before submission.

Academic Integrity

Copied work, shared assessment content, unauthorized answer sites, fabricated evidence or sources, plagiarism, and unapproved AI-generated submissions are prohibited. You may be asked to explain your work or process.

Communication

Messages to your TOR should identify the course, unit, lesson, and page, explain what you attempted, and ask a precise question. For portfolio, presentation, audio/video, publication, or upload problems, include the device, file type, and error message.

Technical Requirements and Course Materials

  • reliable internet and a current browser;
  • Moodle and academy-account access;
  • a method to create readable documents or PDFs;
  • audio/video recording tools when the course requires them;
  • only the sources, tools, and media authorized on the current page.

Accessibility and Accommodations

Approved accommodations apply throughout the course. Contact your TOR if an accommodation is missing from a text, visual, recording, assessment, or submission activity.

Revision and Remediation

When directed, study the feedback, correct the underlying issue, preserve evidence of the revision process, and resubmit through the designated activity. Revision should improve meaning, evidence, organization, craft, delivery, or conventions—not merely replace a final answer.

page.contents:

Course Acknowledgement

Before You Acknowledge

Confirm that you reviewed the Course Overview, How This Course Works, and Expectations and Policies pages. Ask your TOR about anything you do not understand before beginning graded work.

I Understand That

  • this Creative Writing course contains 6 units and 48 lessons in the official Moodle sequence;
  • I must complete lessons, required evidence, checkpoints, quizzes, and Unit Assessments in order;
  • page views alone do not demonstrate completion;
  • the minimum mastery threshold is 80%;
  • revision or remediation may be required;
  • my TOR monitors progress, grades evidence, and provides support.

Student Commitment

I will read directions carefully, complete my own work, preserve organized process evidence, use sources responsibly, review feedback, revise when required, and communicate when I need help.

Evidence and Product Acknowledgement

I understand that a final answer or polished product alone may be insufficient. When required, I will submit annotations, planning, source evidence, drafts, revisions, rehearsal evidence, reflection, or explanation so my learning process can be evaluated.

Academic Integrity Acknowledgement

I understand that copied answers, shared assessment content, plagiarism, fabricated sources or evidence, unauthorized answer sites, and unapproved AI-generated submissions violate course expectations.

Need Help Before Beginning?

Contact your TOR and identify Creative Writing, Course Orientation, this page title, and your exact question. Do not acknowledge the course until the question is resolved.

Acknowledgement Statement

By selecting the acknowledgement response below, I confirm that I reviewed all four orientation pages, understand the workflow and policies, and agree to meet the stated expectations.

Next Step

Submit the acknowledgement response, return to the course, and begin the first required activity in Moodle.
